text: Envelope + LED Lighting scenario Figure 11 shows the impact of the Comprehensive GHP packages on seasonal peak intensity for the median building. In all climate zones and seasons, the peak intensity is reduced further and further as more efficiency measures are added. The Comprehensive GHP + High Efficiency Envelope + LED Lighting package demonstrates the lowest peak intensity of the four scenarios shown for all climate zones and seasons. This indicates that the envelope and lighting measures are lowering the HVAC loads during critical hours of the day throughout the year. 31 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Maximum daily peak intensity by season between the baseline, Comprehensive GHP, Comprehensive GHP + High Efficiency Envelope, and Comprehensive GHP + High Efficiency Envelope + LED Lighting scenario 5.8 Sizing Analysis During each building simulation, the GHEDesigner tool is used to automatically size the ground heat exchanger used in the model based on the annual load of the building. This process is explained in more detail in Section 3.10 as well as the individual measure documentation. When the envelope and lighting measures are combined with the GHP measures, the annual load of a building is reduced due to the efficiency improvements. Therefore, there is an opportunity to reduce the size of the required ground heat exchanger loop for the building. The heat pump unit itself is also resized in the measure after the envelope measures are applied, so it could also be possible to reduce the required capacity of the heat pump. This section compares several ground heat exchanger outputs for the Comprehensive GHP package, Comprehensive GHP + High Efficiency Envelope package, and Comprehensive GHP + High Efficiency Envelope + LED Lighting package. This gives insight into how much the envelope improvements and LED lighting can help reduce ground heat exchanger size, heat pump size, and hence drilling time and cost, for a building installing GHPs. 5.8.1 Ground Heat Exchanger Sizing Figure 12 shows the borehole count, borehole depth, and total length of the ground heat exchanger for the three Comprehensive GHP packages. Because commercial buildings have such 32 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. a wide range of size and load, the borehole count is normalized by building floor area (number of boreholes per thousand feet of floor area). The total ground heat exchanger loop length is calculated by multiplying the number of boreholes by the borehole depth, resulting in a rough approximation for the total length of drilling that would be required for the system. When comparing the three packages, the borehole count, borehole depth, and total ground heat exchanger length get progressively smaller as more efficiency measures are added to the package. While the impact on the median building is rather minimum in all three cases, we see more substantial impacts on the more extreme ends of the box-and-whisker plot.
